Dragon*Con's origins were as a gaming convention. An association named
"DAGR" hosted the first Dragon*Con, many many years ago; the acronym
stood for "Dragon Alliance of Gamers and Role-Players", of which I was a
member.

It has always been, and remains primarily a gaming convention, although
with an inordinate amount of crap tacked on in all directions.

>Any single item from that list may be classified as incidental to the whole (or

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
jspektr wrote:
> Just 20 gaming events? Wow. The largest local Missouri conventions,
> Visioncon and Archon, both have more gaming than that. When a
> bible-belt convention with attendance around 1,000 people has more
> gaming than Dragoncon, I'd have to go with the "not a gaming
> convention" crowd.

If a convention with an attendance around 1,000 does, in fact, have more
gaming than Dragon*Con, I'd be right there with you. But D*C will hold,
if history be any guide, many more than "about 20" events.

Note that what a web site "currently lists" is not on a 1-1 correspondence
to what occurs at the Con.

For example, most, if not all, of the VTES events at Gen*Con are listed
incorrectly or not listed at all on the Gen*Con web site.

For another example, the visioncon website lists a total of 0 game events,
from what I can find. Likewise the Archon web site lists 0 (and says that
the event schedule won't be posted until late August - about 6 weeks prior
to Archon).

What you see on the Dragon*Con is the first events registered trickling
into the web site. Rather than wait until "most" of the events are
in before updating the web site, the D*C staff update it as the events
come in.



1990). What happened 12 years ago has almost no relation to happened

DragonCon could certainly use better web administration and a

to the last 3 of each, so my experiences are current, not 12 years out
of date.

Messages.Author: Ben Peal
Messages.Body:
Andrew S. Davidson
> Derek Ray wrote:
> >Dragon*Con's origins were as a gaming convention. An association named
> >"DAGR" hosted the first Dragon*Con, many many years ago; the acronym
> >stood for "Dragon Alliance of Gamers and Role-Players", of which I was a
> >member.
> >
> >It has always been, and remains primarily a gaming convention, although
> >with an inordinate amount of crap tacked on in all directions.
>
> I haven't been to it since it was also the Origins for that year in
> 1990. That was the only year that I found it worth travelling to. I
> thought it was ok but have since preferred to travel to lots of other
> cons of various sorts. I still pigeonhole it as primarily an SF con
> and its official history confirms this impression.
>
> http://www.dragoncon.org/history.html

Of the few times I've been to DragonCon ('98-'00), it's been pretty
clear that it's first and foremost a sci-fi/fantasy fan con, with the
gaming being secondary. That might not have been how it started out,
but that's the way it is now.

That being said, I've had an absolute blast playing in V:TES events
and non-V:TES gaming events at DragonCon every year I've been there.
On top of that, I've been able to see a bunch of goth bands (along
with Gwar), see lots of hot women in cool outfits, and eat great sushi
and other fine dinners with the V:TES crew.

Yeah, the North American Championships are at GenCon, and the V:TES
there is awesome, but for me DragonCon provides more overall fun.

Seeya there in August!

- Ben Peal, Prince of Boston
fu...@mindstorm.com
